approach: Add one module, crates/athena-core/src/followups.rs, and call it from one line of `Athena::close_dispatched` (run/close.rs), the one place every job that ran closes. The module holds: (1) `is_follow_up(item)`, a directive-phrase matcher on whole words ('as its own job/request', 'as a separate request', 'as a follow-up request', 'propose ... follow-up/request'), not bare words. (2) `chain_root`, which walks the retry chain through `retried_job` ('try again on <job>' in each job's request text, the same link `retry_target` follows at preflight.rs:300-329) to the first job. (3) `queue(..)`, a pure function that keeps directive items, drops duplicates, items already queued for the chain's root, items that name a record id already in the records, and anything over the cap of 5 counted across the whole chain. It builds each request through the existing `RequestQueue::apply` on a `ProposedChange`, so `StewardRequest::new` (steward.rs:535) stays the only request-text builder. (4) `Athena::follow_up_files`, which loads `Records` at HEAD, calls `queue` and returns the `NewFile`s. They are added to `closing.files`, so they go in the same closing commit as the outcome on every non-hold close. No new record type, config key, crate or dependency. Answers to the five findings: (1) close.rs is kept as a one-line deliverable, because manage.rs is `athena close` for jobs that did not finish (decision 1). (2) Dedupe and cap now key on the retry chain's root, found through `retried_job`, not `previous_job` (which is the latest landed job, not the retry link: chain.rs:1, scope_guard.rs:639), and a failed-job-then-retry test is added. (3) Bare words are replaced by directive phrases, items naming an id already in the records are skipped, and a table test uses this brief's real out_of_scope list. (4) The request text gets an 'Original job: <root> — <title>' line. (5) Criterion 2 is split into two named tests that one filter runs.

decisions.choice: Hook in run/close.rs `close_dispatched`, one call line `closing.files.extend(self.follow_up_files(ctx.reading, ctx.ui));` right after `push_closing_records(&mut closing);` (close.rs:38). Add run/close.rs to the file list; leave manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs unedited unless a compile error shows a need, and the producer says so in its report. Answer to finding 1.
decisions.reason: The reading says manage.rs is where a job closes and the producer must confirm it. Confirmed against the code: manage.rs `close` (manage.rs:74) and `close_with` (manage.rs:82) are the person's `athena close` for a job that did not finish (Queued or Proposed become Dropped, Declined, Blocked become Abandoned, interrupted Dispatched become Abandoned after `recover_interrupted`, manage.rs:240). A job that ran closes only through `close_dispatched` (close.rs:8), so the fgwz case never passes manage.rs. The logic and glue are in followups.rs, so the edit outside the reading's list is one line, and the scope is the same: queue follow-ups when a job ends with a reading. If a scope guard refuses the close.rs edit, the producer reports it and does not route around it.

rejected.option: Hook in manage.rs `close_with`, to stay inside the listed deliverables
rejected.why: It sees only jobs closed by hand, never a job that ran to an outcome, so criterion 1 (the fgwz case) would not hold; it would also queue work from jobs a person abandoned before they started.

rejected.option: A steward scan that queues follow-ups for every closed job with a reading
rejected.why: It runs on a later pass, not when the job ends, and would backfill historical jobs including fgwz, which the brief puts out of scope.

rejected.option: Queue after the closing commit as a second records commit
rejected.why: The outcome could land without its follow-ups if the second commit fails. One commit is atomic, and the dedupe check reads records already at HEAD.

decisions.choice: Idempotence and cap key on the root of the retry chain. `chain_root(records, closing_job)` loops at most 16 times, reading each job's `request.text` with `crate::reading::retried_job(records, text)` (reading/retry.rs:201, re-exported by `pub use retry::*`, reading.rs:70) and stopping at a cycle, an unknown job or a job whose request is not 'try again on <job>', as `retry_target` does (preflight.rs:300-329). The key line is `Out-of-scope item key: <root id> <first 16 hex of athena_data::sha256_hex(lowercased, whitespace-collapsed item)>`. `queue` drops an item whose key line is already in the text of any REQUEST_CHANNEL request in the records, and subtracts the count of distinct existing requests holding `Out-of-scope item key: <root id> ` from MAX_PER_JOB = 5. Answer to finding 2.
decisions.reason: A failed job that a person or the drain retries is the usual path, and the retry gets a new reading and a new id. Keyed on the closing job's own id, the retry would queue every item a second time. The retry link in this code is the 'try again on <job>' request text (reading.rs:1307 `RETRY_PREFIX`; retry_reference, retry.rs:560), not `previous_job`: `previous_job` is the latest job landed in the base's history (chain.rs:1; scope_guard.rs:639 says it is not used for this). A job the preflight stopped retries its target (preflight.rs:295-300), so the chain stays consistent. Records at HEAD are the source of truth. The job lock is held while a job closes, so no other writer adds keys between the check and the commit. A re-entry for the same job id (the 'branch kept moving' bail, close.rs:601) finds nothing at HEAD from the failed commit and queues the same files; land_or_block clones `closing.files` per attempt (close.rs:272), so ids are stable across attempts. A held job (`commit_hold`, close.rs:216) never reaches the hook and queues nothing, so its resume queues once under the held job's root.

rejected.option: Key on the closing job's own id (the earlier plan)
rejected.why: A failed-then-retried job queues each item again, so 'retrying the same job twice yields each follow-up once' fails.

rejected.option: Follow `previous_job` back to the first job
rejected.why: `previous_job` is the latest landed job in the base's history, not the retried job (chain.rs:1; scope_guard.rs:639), so it names the wrong job for a retry.

rejected.option: Call `earlier_jobs` (reading/retry.rs:588)
rejected.why: It is `pub(super)`, so followups.rs cannot call it. A 16-step loop over the public `retried_job` is about ten lines and mirrors `retry_target`.

rejected.option: Dedupe on the item text alone across all jobs
rejected.why: The same wording from two unrelated jobs would collapse into one request; the brief asks for one per job (chain) and item.

decisions.choice: `is_follow_up(item)` matches directive phrases on whole words, not subject-matter words. Normalise: lowercase, split on every character that is not alphanumeric or '-', join with single spaces. Then it is a follow-up when (a) some word 'as' is followed by an optional determiner (a, an, its, their) and then ('own' or 'separate') plus a noun (job, jobs, request, requests, work), or a follow-up word (follow-up, follow-ups, followup, followups) with an optional noun, or (b) the word 'propose' or 'proposes' is followed within three words by a follow-up word or by request(s) or job(s). Both lists are consts. Bare 'follow-ups', 'proposal', 'separate request' without 'as' never match. Answer to finding 3 (wording part).
decisions.reason: In this codebase 'follow-up', 'proposal' and 'propose' are domain words, so bare words give false positives. On this brief's own out_of_scope list, the items 'Reprioritizing queued follow-ups ahead of or behind other work', 'Backfilling the follow-ups already lost from job ...-fgwz ...' and '... a separate request from introspection ...-pj25' have no 'as ...' directive and no 'propose', so none queues. The fgwz-style 'Propose these as follow-up requests: ...' matches (a) and (b), and 'Plan critic memory runs as its own job' matches (a). A plain list such as 'athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, docs/decisions.md and records/' matches nothing. It runs only on an already accepted reading and is not a `check_*` step, so it changes which readings are accepted in no case and adds no refusal rule.

rejected.option: Bare markers (propose, follow-ups, separate request), the earlier plan
rejected.why: They queue the brief's own exclusions and the already-filed pj25 item.

rejected.option: Queue every out_of_scope item
rejected.why: A plain exclusion list would become a meaningless request.

rejected.option: Ask a model to classify the items
rejected.why: It adds a role and cost, and the result is not deterministic, so dedupe and tests would not be reliable.

rejected.option: Match a bare first word 'queue' or 'propose'
rejected.why: 'Queue order and the backlog hold' is a noun phrase in the fgwz list; a first-word rule would queue it.

decisions.choice: After a directive match, skip an item that names a full record id (`crate::reading::job_ids_in(item)`, topics.rs:9) that is a job in `records.jobs` or an `IntrospectionRecord.id` in `records.introspections` (introspection.rs:185-186), other than the ids of the closing job's own chain. The skip is a `skipped` entry and a ui line 'skipped: names <id>, already in the records'. Answer to finding 3 (filed-elsewhere part).
decisions.reason: The code can answer 'is this work filed?' by looking the id up in Records, so no open question is needed. An item that cites an existing job or introspection points at work that has a record; the chain's own ids are excluded because an item may cite the job it came from. The cost is that a directive item citing an unrelated existing job is not queued; the ui line shows it so a person can ask for it by hand (risk 3).

rejected.option: Queue it and ask the user (the earlier plan's open question)
rejected.why: The code can look the id up, so the question is settled by reading records.

rejected.option: Treat a cited job as filed only when a steward request cites it
rejected.why: The text of other requests is a weaker signal than the record's existence and would need a second text search.

decisions.choice: Build each request with `RequestQueue.apply(&ProposedChange{kind: WorkItemKind::Proposal, key: <item key>, title: <title>, rung: Ladder::Implementation, source: Reference::job(<closing job>), evidence: vec![Reference::job(<root>)], request: <text>, brief: None}, &taken)`. `taken` is the set of job ids in the loaded records plus the ids made so far.
decisions.reason: These are all the fields of `ProposedChange` (steward.rs:305-319). `RequestQueue` is a unit struct (steward.rs:660); `apply` (steward.rs:663-683) runs `StewardRequest::from_change`, which calls `StewardRequest::new` (steward.rs:535) and writes the `Request` record on REQUEST_CHANNEL (steward.rs:335). One request-text builder and one Request writer are reused, which is criterion 5. When the text names no path, `from_change` falls back to the source if it is a path, else `records/` (steward.rs:626-634); a job reference is not a path, so the Files line is `records/`, as the brief assumes.

rejected.option: Call `StewardRequest::new` and build the `Request` record in followups.rs
rejected.why: It duplicates id generation, record writing and the error mapping already in `RequestQueue::apply`.

rejected.option: A new record type or marker file for follow-ups
rejected.why: The brief rules out new record types; a key line in the text is enough to dedupe.

decisions.choice: Request text: line 1 is the title (the item on one line, bullet marker stripped, cut at a char boundary to about 90 chars). Body lines: `Queued from the out_of_scope list of job <closing id>.`; `Original job: <root id> — <root job's latest reading title>` (falls back to the closing reading's title); `Original request: <first line of the root job's request, cut to about 120 chars>`; `Item: <item on one line>`; `Out-of-scope item key: <root id> <16 hex>`; then `Acceptance:` with two `- ` bullets (the named work is done with no unrelated change; fmt, clippy and test pass). The title and request context lines are included only when `followed_up_ids(line)` and `dependency_ids_in(line)` find nothing in them. The text never writes 'follow up', 'follow-up', 'Depends on' or 'try again on' next to an id. Answer to finding 4.
decisions.reason: The context lines make the request stand on its own: an item such as 'Propose these as follow-up requests: queue order and the backlog hold' depends on the original reading for its meaning. `followed_up_ids` (topics.rs:479-506) reads the id that comes right after 'follow up', 'follow-up', 'followup', 'follows up' or 'following up' (FOLLOW_UP_PHRASES, topics.rs:467), with only on, of, to, job, the, earlier between. A job found there is one the reading must account for, and a reading that ignores it is refused by `check_prior_result_and_scope` (corpus case `follow-up-on-a-job-the-reading-ignores`). `dependency_ids_in` (topics.rs:25) reads only a 'Depends on' line and `retried_job` only a request that starts 'try again on'. With none of those, `job_ids_in` still carries the original job to the reader as evidence (`referenced_jobs`, topics.rs:533-560, at most MAX_REFERENCED_JOBS = 3), the cited-not-relied-on shape (corpus case `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying`). A job title that says 'follow up on job <id>' would break that, hence the per-line guard. An item whose own words do so is quoted as written.

rejected.option: Write 'Follow-up from job <id>.' and a `followup-<job>-<hash>` key
rejected.why: Both put the phrase 'follow-up' in the text, a fragile near-match for `followed_up_ids`.

rejected.option: Add a `Depends on <id>` line
rejected.why: The original job is already closed, so a dependency line adds an open question and a plan edge for no gain.

rejected.option: Title and generic acceptance only (the earlier plan)
rejected.why: The reader sees little about what the original job was; the critic's finding 4.

decisions.choice: Put the follow-up files in `closing.files` only and leave the `trailers` vector unchanged.
decisions.reason: `trailers` also feeds the landing commit message (close.rs:109-117). An `Athena-Job` trailer naming a request job whose closing records the landing does not add refuses the landing (invariant.rs:406-422). The closing commit already names its own existing job, which satisfies `names_existing_work` (invariant.rs:845-859).

rejected.option: One `Athena-Job` trailer per queued follow-up, as the steward does
rejected.why: The steward's commit is records-only; here the same vector is cloned into the landing commit, which would refuse.

decisions.choice: `queue` is a pure function over values: the reading's items, the closing and root ids, the root's title and request line, the texts of existing REQUEST_CHANNEL requests, the set of known record ids (jobs and introspections), and `taken`. `Athena::follow_up_files` extracts those from `Records` at HEAD. It returns early with no work when no item passes `is_follow_up`, and any failure to read HEAD or load records prints one ui line and returns an empty list; it never fails the close.
decisions.reason: Unit tests then need no git repository or `Records` fixture, and the end-to-end tests in run/tests.rs and drain.rs cover the Records path. Records is loaded once per close that has a follow-up item; `score_on` already loads Records at HEAD per attempt (close.rs:24).

rejected.option: `queue(records, reading, taken)` over `Records`
rejected.why: Unit tests would need to build `Records` by hand (many fields, store.rs:246-273); the chain and key logic would only be testable end to end.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/followups.rs. Define `MAX_PER_JOB = 5`, the const list of directive nouns and follow-up words, and `is_follow_up` (normalise: lowercase, split on every character that is not alphanumeric or '-', join with single spaces; then rule (a) `as` + optional determiner + (own|separate) + noun, or follow-up word with optional noun; rule (b) propose|proposes within three words of a follow-up word or request(s)/job(s)). Define `follow_up_key(root, item)` as `<root id> <first 16 hex of athena_data::sha256_hex(lowercased, whitespace-collapsed item bytes)>`.

In followups.rs define `chain_root(records, closing: &JobId) -> (JobId, Vec<JobId>)`: loop at most 16 times, read the current job's `request.text`, call `crate::reading::retried_job(records, text)`, stop at a cycle, an unknown job or no link; return the root and the chain. Mirror `retry_target` (preflight.rs:300-329).

In followups.rs define the pure `queue(input) -> Plan{files, jobs, skipped}`. Inputs: the reading's out_of_scope items, the closing and root ids, the root's title and first request line, the texts of existing REQUEST_CHANNEL requests, the set of known record ids (jobs and introspection ids, minus the chain's own), and `taken`. Steps: collapse each item to one line with bullet markers stripped; keep `is_follow_up` items; drop duplicate keys; drop keys already in an existing text; skip an item whose `job_ids_in(item)` names a known id; subtract the count of distinct existing requests holding `Out-of-scope item key: <root> ` from MAX_PER_JOB; for each remaining item build the text of decision 6, build a `ProposedChange` (kind Proposal, key, title cut at a char boundary to about 90 chars, rung Implementation, source `Reference::job(closing)`, evidence `Reference::job(root)`, brief None), call `RequestQueue.apply(&change,&taken)` (steward.rs:660-683), add each made job id to `taken`, and turn an `Err` or a skip into a `skipped` entry. Include the title and request context lines only when `followed_up_ids(line)` and `dependency_ids_in(line)` are empty for that line.

In followups.rs add `impl Athena { pub(crate) fn follow_up_files(&self, reading: &Reading, ui: &dyn Ui) -> Vec<NewFile> }`. Return early with nothing when no item passes `is_follow_up`. Otherwise load `Records` at `self.head()` (lib.rs:273), compute `chain_root`, collect the texts of requests on REQUEST_CHANNEL and the known ids, call `queue`, print one ui line per queued or skipped item (with the reason: already queued, names <id>, over the cap of 5, refused text), and return the files. A failure to read HEAD or load Records prints one line and returns an empty list; it never fails the close.

risks.risk: A directive item that cites an unrelated existing job or introspection id is skipped as 'filed elsewhere', so real follow-up work could be left unqueued (for example 'propose closing <job id> as its own request' where that job exists).
risks.mitigation: The skip prints a ui line naming the id and the item, so a person sees it and can queue it by hand; the table test pins the behavior on this brief's pj25 and fgwz ids. The chain's own ids are exempt so an item may cite the job it came from.

risks.risk: The directive phrases can still queue an item that is really an exclusion (for example 'treat the proposal as its own request').
risks.mitigation: Whole-word directive matching, the cap of 5 across a chain, key dedupe, and a ui line per queued request; the lists are two consts covered by a table test; a wrong request is closed with `athena close`.

risks.risk: A retry whose reading rephrases the items gets new keys and queues them again, since dedupe is by item wording.
risks.mitigation: The cap of 5 is counted across the whole chain, so the duplicate cost is bounded; wording-independent dedupe is not planned and would need a similarity rule.

risks.risk: The closing commit now adds job directories that hold only a request.json. A gate rule, the history check or `athena check` could object when the closing commit is not the steward's.
risks.mitigation: Read: `closing_jobs` counts only candidate, verification and outcome files (invariant.rs:240-269) and `landing` checks only the landed job (386-446). The end-to-end test commits through the real gate on a branch with an intervention commit and a records-only commit; if the gate refuses, the producer reports it and does not weaken a rule.

risks.risk: The queued text could be read by `followed_up_ids` as continuing the original job, and the follow-up's own reading would then be refused by `check_prior_result_and_scope` when the drain reads it. The new title and request context lines raise this risk.
risks.mitigation: The text writes no follow-up phrase before an id; context lines are included only when `followed_up_ids` and `dependency_ids_in` find nothing in them; a unit test asserts the three finders return nothing on each queued text; the two corpus cases run in `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: The Files line falls back to `records/` when the item names no path, and a reader may treat `records/` as a governance area.
risks.mitigation: This is the brief's stated fallback and matches `from_change` (steward.rs:626-634). The reader makes its own deliverable list from the request, so Files is a hint, not a limit.

risks.risk: run/close.rs is outside the reading's listed deliverables, while manage.rs, steward.rs and reading.rs are listed and left unedited.
risks.mitigation: The edit is one call line and the logic is in followups.rs; manage.rs is shown (manage.rs:74-159, 240) not to be the close path for a job that ran. If a scope guard refuses the close.rs edit, the producer reports it and does not route around it.

risks.risk: Test fixtures need words from the boundary lists, and the boundary scan fails any tracked file that names them.
risks.mitigation: The tests build them at run time from `athena_context::briefs::boundary_words()` and `boundary_fragments()`, as briefs.rs:2369 does; `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` runs in `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: Loading `Records` at HEAD adds cost to a close.
risks.mitigation: `follow_up_files` returns before loading when no out_of_scope item passes `is_follow_up`; `score_on` already loads Records at HEAD per closing attempt (close.rs:24).

All five non-hold outcomes (landed, rejected, failed, blocked, stale) pass the line before the landing branch (close.rs:105) and the plain commit (close.rs:132).

dependents.reason: Not edited and not a hook: it closes jobs that did not finish (never ran or interrupted) and queues nothing. Unchanged behavior; `cargo test -p athena-core` runs the existing manage tests.

dependents.name: commit shape of closing and landing commits, which now also add other jobs' request.json
dependents.test: followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_of_a_closed_job commits through the real gate (`build_commit` inside `land_or_block`, close.rs:333; `commit_records_with` for the others) on a branch holding an intervention commit and the ask records-only commit; `cargo test --locked` also runs athena-gate's own tests, since no classification function changes.
dependents.reason: None of these functions changes, so no other crate's tests are re-targeted. `closing_jobs` counts only candidate.json, verification.json, outcome.json and outcome-landed.json, so a directory with only request.json is not a closing job and adds no SeveralJobs refusal. `landing` checks only the landed job's files and an Athena-Job trailer, and the trailer vector is unchanged (decision 7). The ordering rule fires on a later record that lacks request.json; a directory with only request.json is the first record a job has, as `athena ask --later` and the steward write it (steward.rs:1427-1430). Commit-shape table: (1) job landing: code, closing records and follow-up requests; valid, one closing job. (2) records-only closing (rejected, failed, blocked, stale): fingerprint unchanged, Athena-Job names the existing job, `names_existing_work` passes. (3) intervention commit: unchanged, queues nothing. (4) steward records-only commit that adds request-only jobs: unchanged, the same file shape. (5) hold commit: unchanged, queues nothing. (6) retry-after-block landing (`outcome-landed.json`): not through `close_dispatched`, queues nothing; the blocked close before it queued them. (7) `athena close` of a job that never ran: unchanged.

demonstrations.method: Two tests share the prefix `followups_queue_one_request`, so one filter runs both. (a) `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_pure` in followups.rs is a table over `queue(..)` with this brief's real out_of_scope list plus fgwz-style items. (b) `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_of_a_closed_job` in run/tests.rs closes a real job. Plan step 6 adds `script_with_out_of_scope(items)` (base_script() at run/tests.rs:223-284 with its out_of_scope taken from `items`; `base_script()` calls it with `["Other files"]`). The test builds `athena_with(&repo,&state,PASSES,crate::test_support::plenty_of_space,script_with_out_of_scope(["Propose these as follow-up requests: queue order and the backlog hold","Plan critic memory runs as its own job","athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, docs/decisions.md and records/"]))`. For a realistic branch it first commits one intervention with `athena.intervene(&InterveneArgs{what,why,class:"docs",category:"mistake",job:None,with_staged:false},&Quiet)` (manage.rs:313; the same literal is used at crates/athena-cli/tests/auditor.rs:239), then runs `finished_job(&athena)` (run/tests.rs:2106). The branch then holds the ask records-only commit, the intervention commit and the job landing carrying the two follow-up requests. It differs from the real repository in being a one-job temporary repository with no `athena/records` cutover, so `names_existing_work` is exercised, not `trailers_stopped` (invariant.rs:149-153).
demonstrations.observes: (a) For the fgwz-style directives 'Propose these as follow-up requests: queue order and the backlog hold' and 'Plan critic memory runs as its own job', `queue` returns one file and one job each. For this brief's own list ('Reprioritizing queued follow-ups ahead of or behind other work'; 'Backfilling the follow-ups already lost from job 20261114-034034-fgwz ...'; 'a separate request from introspection 20261114-052207-pj25'; the athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows list) it returns none. (b) The job is Landed. `Records::load(&athena.git,&athena.head()?)` holds exactly 2 new request jobs besides the original, each with a request on channel `REQUEST_CHANNEL`; each request text contains the original job id and an `Out-of-scope item key:` line; `request_text_acceptance(text)` is a non-empty list and `request_text_touches(text)` is non-empty (the builder is `StewardRequest::new`, so it accepted them); `dependency_ids_in(text)`, `followed_up_ids(text)` are empty and `retried_job(&records,text)` is None. The producer also runs `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` to show the reading gate is unchanged: the cases read are `follow-up-on-a-job-the-reading-ignores` (refusal_corpus.rs:1938), `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying` (1925) and `delivery-verb-out-of-scope-shared-helpers-refused` / `-release-notes-refused` / `-names-it-accepted` (989, 998, 1031).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the call in `close_dispatched` no Request records are written and the count of 2 in (b) fails. If `is_follow_up` ignored the 'as ... own job' or 'propose' directive, the counts in (a) and (b) drop below 2. If it matched bare 'follow-ups' or 'separate request', the table in (a) would queue the brief's exclusions.

demonstrations.method: Four tests share the prefix `followups_are_queued_once`, so one filter runs all of them. (1) `followups_are_queued_once_and_capped_pure` in followups.rs: `queue` on a reading with 3 distinct follow-up items, then again with the first call's request texts passed as the existing texts; a reading with 7 items queues 5 and a second call queues 0; a reading that repeats one item twice queues it once; with 5 keys already held under a root, a retry with a new item queues 0 (the cap counts the chain). (2) `followups_are_queued_once_on_reclose` in run/tests.rs: after `finished_job` with 3 follow-up items, load `Records` at the new HEAD and run the production hook's inputs again (`follow_up_files` on the same reading) and see an empty result; this is the state a re-close of the same job id meets. (3) `followups_are_queued_once_across_a_failed_job_and_its_retry` in run/tests.rs: `athena_with(&repo,&state,FAILS_ON_EDIT,crate::test_support::plenty_of_space,script_with_out_of_scope(<3 follow-up items>))` (FAILS_ON_EDIT, run/tests.rs:103, makes the job Failed once the producer edits README.md, as the loop at 4112 and the test at 4060-4074 show); `finished_job` gives the Failed first job and its 3 follow-ups; then `athena.ask(&format!("try again on {first}"),&Quiet)` and `athena.go(..)` on the retry (the form at run/tests.rs:4078-4085), which also fails and closes through `close_dispatched` with the same out_of_scope. (4) `followups_are_queued_once_when_a_held_job_is_retried` in run/tests.rs uses `athena_with(...,crate::test_support::low_once_verifying, script_with_out_of_scope(..))` as `low_disk_before_the_verifier_holds_the_job_and_a_retry_resumes_it` does (run/tests.rs:4390-4401), then `athena.retry(..)` and `go`.
demonstrations.observes: (1) Each key appears in exactly one request; the number of requests under one root equals its distinct follow-up items, at most 5; the second call and the capped call return empty plans. (2) The re-close plan is empty. (3) After the retry closes, loading `Records` at HEAD shows each of the 3 `Out-of-scope item key: <first job id> <hash>` lines in exactly one REQUEST_CHANNEL request, 3 request jobs in all, and the retry's closing commit adds no new request (the retry job's id is not in any key line). (4) The held job's `go` returns the LowDisk hold and the records hold no steward-channel job; after the retry's `go` the follow-ups exist once and carry the held job's id as root.
demonstrations.fails_without: Keyed on the closing job's own id, test (3) finds 6 requests, not 3. Without the key scan, the second `queue` call in (1) and the re-close in (2) add duplicates. Without the cap, the 7-item reading queues 7. If the hook ran in `commit_hold`, the held job in (4) would already have requests.

demonstrations.method: On the final tree run, in this order, the three checks Athena runs: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`. `cargo test --locked` includes `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` (the boundary scan over tracked files, which the new test texts must pass: banned words are built from `athena_context::briefs::boundary_words()` and `boundary_fragments()`, never written out). These supplement the behavior tests of criteria 1-4.
demonstrations.observes: All three commands exit 0. The run includes the new tests named in criteria 1-4 and every existing test in run/tests.rs that goes through `base_script()`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `close_dispatched` call, `followups_queue_one_request_per_follow_up_item_of_a_closed_job` fails and `cargo test --locked` exits non-zero. A line over rustfmt width in followups.rs, or an unused const (MAX_PER_JOB or a marker list left unused), makes `cargo fmt --all --check` or `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` exit non-zero. If the `base_script()` change altered its default reading, existing tests in run/tests.rs would fail. If `pub mod followups;` is missing from lib.rs, its tests are not built and the criterion 1-4 filters match nothing.
